 Run models larger than your RAM or VRAM. InferSSD builds on llama.cpp to run large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models from SSD, using standard GGUF files, with browser chat and an OpenAI-compatible API. It runs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and Qwen3.8 Flash Next in many quantizations, as well as Muse-Spark-Open , Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Gemma4 E4B .

These are the tested GGUF files, used as their publishers released them. Expand a model for its files.

 Performance benchmarks

 4K prompt tier · 256 output tokens · decode measured over tokens 129–256. All rates are in token/s ; higher is faster. The multiple next to each InferSSD rate is its speedup over llama.cpp on the same hardware. On every machine, llama.cpp and InferSSD run DeepSeek's mrfakename Q8 0 and Muse's Unsloth UD-Q4 K XL; on the MacBook Pro they run them with Metal, and Colibri runs the official Safetensors on CPU. See measurement details.

install.title: Get started
install.html:
Desktop app. WiCi Infer is a free app for macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (x64), built on InferSSD. It sets up the engine, downloads models and runs chat, with no terminal. Download for macOS · Download for Windows

Command line. On macOS or Linux:

curl -fsSL https://github.com/wici-ai/inferssd/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh

On Windows, in PowerShell:

irm https://github.com/wici-ai/inferssd/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex

On macOS 15 or later on Apple silicon and on Windows 10 or 11 x64, the installer downloads the release's prebuilt macOS or Windows package, with no developer tools. On Linux it builds the release from source for the machine's CPU and GPU, which takes about 2 to 12 minutes and needs Git, Python 3.9 or later, a C/C++ compiler, systemd with cgroup v2, and the CUDA toolkit or the ROCm HIP SDK for the GPU. The installer works in a private environment and uses no sudo. Follow the printed PATH instruction if it shows one.

Then start a model:

# Chat in your terminal
inferssd cli -hf mrfakename/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF

# Or start the web UI and an OpenAI-compatible API at http://127.0.0.1:8080
inferssd serve -hf mrfakename/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF

-hf downloads and runs mrfakename/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF (Q8_0), unsloth/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-GGUF (UD-Q4_K_XL), unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF (UD-Q4_K_XL), bartowski/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF (IQ4_XS) and google/gemma-4-E4B-it-qat-q4_0-gguf. For any other file in Models, download all of its files to one folder and pass the first with -m:

hf download unsloth/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-GGUF --include "UD-IQ1_S/*" --local-dir ~/models/deepseek
inferssd serve -m ~/models/deepseek/UD-IQ1_S/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017-UD-IQ1_S-00001-of-00005.gguf

With serve, open http://127.0.0.1:8080 in your browser, or point any OpenAI-compatible client at http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1. Add --host 0.0.0.0 to reach it from other devices on your network; the API has no authentication, so anyone who can reach the port can use it.

The first -hf run downloads the model files to ~/.local/share/inferssd/models (%LOCALAPPDATA%\inferssd\models on Windows) and measures your machine. Use --model-dir /path/on/ssd to choose the drive. There is no memory setting to choose: InferSSD uses the memory available. Stop with Ctrl+C, or /exit in chat.

See the quick start for upgrades and uninstalling.
